Build a compatible data frame for forest plots

Source: R/forest_df.R
forest_df.Rd

Creates the tabular input used by forest_reg() from uni_reg(), multi_reg(), and optionally descriptive_table() objects. This function is useful when users want to inspect, edit, or reuse the exact data that will be passed to the forest plot. Stratified regression objects are also supported when supplied one at a time; the returned data frame keeps the characteristic rows once and places strata side by side as separate effect columns for forest_reg().

Usage

forest_df(uni = NULL, multi = NULL, desc = NULL, digits = 2)

Arguments

uni

A gtregression regression object, usually the crude results (for example uni_reg(), cox_reg(), conditional_logit_reg() or ordinal_reg()). If multi is supplied without uni, the adjusted object is plotted as a single effect column.

multi

Optional adjusted object of the same model family, for example multi_reg() or a model fitted with multivariable = TRUE. Exposure-specific adjusted results (adjust_for) and the single multivariable model can also be shown together; the second column is then labelled "Mutually adjusted".

desc

Optional descriptive table object from descriptive_table().

digits

Number of digits used when formatting confidence intervals.

Value

A data frame with display columns, formatted effect-size columns, standard-error columns, and plotting attributes used by forest_reg() to draw confidence intervals.

Details

Effect columns use the same header as the source tables, for example "Matched OR (95% CI)" for conditional_logit_reg() and "Common OR (95% CI)" for ordinal_reg(), and the estimates and intervals are taken unchanged from each result's table_body.

Examples

birthwt_data <- data_birthwt |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    smoke = factor(smoke, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    ht = factor(ht, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    low = factor(low, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Normal BW", "Low BW"))
  )

uni_or <- uni_reg(
  birthwt_data,
  outcome = "low",
  exposures = c("age", "lwt", "smoke", "ht"),
  approach = "logit"
)
#> Outcome `low`: modelling the event 'Low BW' (second level); reference level is 'Normal BW'.
multi_or <- multi_reg(
  birthwt_data,
  outcome = "low",
  exposures = c("smoke", "ht"),
  adjust_for = c("age", "lwt"),
  approach = "logit"
)
#> Outcome `low`: modelling the event 'Low BW' (second level); reference level is 'Normal BW'.

forest_data <- forest_df(uni_or, multi_or)
head(forest_data)
#>   Characteristic                                              OR (95% CI)
#> 1            age                                         0.95 (0.89–1.01)
#> 2            lwt                                         0.99 (0.97–1.00)
#> 3          smoke                                                         
#> 4             No                                                     Ref.
#> 5            Yes                                         2.02 (1.08–3.78)
#> 6             ht                                                         
#>                                           Adjusted OR (95% CI)      se_uni
#> 1                                                              0.031513763
#> 2                                                              0.006169588
#> 3                                                                       NA
#> 4                                                         Ref.          NA
#> 5                                             1.96 (1.03–3.70) 0.319642287
#> 6                                                                       NA
#>      se_adj
#> 1        NA
#> 2        NA
#> 3        NA
#> 4        NA
#> 5 0.3258778
#> 6        NA
